With yaw=0 and the trunk straight ahead, Godot's Vector2.rotated(-60 deg) turns (0,-1) into u=(-0.866,-0.5). The mouth -u points right and toward the player, so the notch itself is correct. The problem is the haft. Its horizontal part is (-u.y, u.x) = (0.5,-0.866), scaled by cos(HAFT_RISE=22 deg)=0.927. Projecting h0 against v in _arc_pose leaves that horizontal part unchanged, because it is already perpendicular to u3, and `square` is perpendicular to v.

Positions below are relative to the trunk axis at the cut height, with the eye at (0,0.8):
- 0.42 axe: grip = hit - h0*head_at ≈ (-0.11, 0.39), arc centre ≈ (-0.27, 0.67).
- 0.82 axe: grip ≈ (-0.29, 0.71), and the centre ≈ (-0.43, 0.95) sits behind the camera.

The basis in _arc_pose is Basis(x, d=h0, -w), so the pivot's +Y is the haft. _build_hand puts the forearm capsule (y=-0.13) and the cuff (y=-0.24) along the pivot's -Y. At impact (EMBED, 0.22 s on every hit) and through the arc, the right forearm therefore points along -h0: down, left and back toward the camera. The right shoulder (SHOULDER x=+0.2; HandR rest x=+0.28) is to the right and back. The arm is drawn about 60-65 deg off the line to the right shoulder, and on every hit it reads as a cross-body or left-handed arm.

This came with the change. The old haft (u.y,0,-u.x) with u=(0,-1) gave (-1,0,0), so the forearm pointed right, which was correct. The head path itself is fine: at +55 deg on the arc the head is to the right of the centre and moves along u3 to the left. Only the arm and hand placement is wrong. It is purely cosmetic and does not affect the server cut or the fall.

I would not take the reviewer's second suggestion (rotating haft_h toward the right). var sh := ChopAim.shoulder(_actor.global_position, _actor.rotation.y)
var g := _pivot.global_position
var dir := (sh - g).normalized()
